title: Longest Block Where Nothing Repeats Too Often

concept.title: A window with a map of counts
body: You look for the longest block of consecutive elements in which **no value occurs more than `k` times**. Use a sliding window with a map of the counts of the values inside it. Add the element at the right end. If its count is now more than `k`, shrink the window from the left until that count is `k` again.
Only the value `x` that was just added can break the rule, so it is enough to shrink while `count[x] > k`. Both ends only move forward, so the work is linear.

statement: Given `n` integers and a number `k`, find the length of the longest block of consecutive elements in which every value occurs at most `k` times.

examples.note: The block 1 2 3 1 2 3 has every value twice: length 6.

hints: Keep a window and a map with the counts of its values.
After adding the new element, shrink from the left while its count is above k.

explanation: The window keeps the counts of its values; when the newest value is too frequent, the left end moves until the count drops back to `k`.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
l = 0
best = 0
for rr, x in enumerate(a):
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
    while count[x] > k:
        count[a[l]] -= 1
        l += 1
    best = max(best, rr - l + 1)
print(best)
